title: Enhanced Perturbation with Outermost Layer Seeding
scientific_hypothesis: Increasing optimizer perturbation magnitude to ±25 nm and selectively seeding perturbations on outermost 4 layers (indices 0-3) will break the symmetry of quarter-wave initialization, enabling escape from local minima and improved coupling to higher-order Fabry-Perot resonances in the 450-650 nm band.
design_principle: Larger perturbation steps during gradient optimization can overcome shallow local minima; outermost layers dominate boundary condition matching and standing wave field distribution.
proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating TiO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate, starting with TiO2 (high-index) at air interface, ending with SiO2 at substrate interface
design_variables: all 24 layer thicknesses with ±25 nm initial perturbation on layers 0-3, ±10 nm on layers 4-23
soft_objectives: maintain or improve robustness score above 0.528
minimize crosstalk between visible and NIR bands
theory_basis: Quarter-wave baseline initialization provides physically motivated starting point; needle optimization principle supports iterative layer adjustment
expected_advantages: Breaks symmetry of previous route_01 initialization
Explores different region of thickness configuration space
May access higher-order resonances missed by smaller perturbations
known_risks: Larger perturbations may reduce convergence stability
May not improve upon 0.9800 if already near global optimum
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer TiO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate at 45 degrees incidence. Initialize from quarter-wave thicknesses at 675 nm center wavelength. Apply gradient thickness optimization with perturbation schedule: layers 0-3 receive ±25 nm initial step magnitude, layers 4-23 receive ±10 nm initial step magnitude. Target high reflectance in 450-650 nm band and high transmittance in 700-1000 nm band. Evaluate unpolarized light (average of s and p polarization). Maximum 24 layers fixed. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 450-650 nm, 700-1000 nm. soft objectives: high reflectance in 450-650 nm; high transmittance in 700-1000 nm; minimized crosstalk between bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 450-650 nm; reflectance in 700-1000 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 24 layers.
revision_reason: Directly implements feedback directive to increase perturbation magnitude and seed outermost layers; differs from route_01 which used uniform smaller perturbations
